end.summary:
Practised multiplying numbers ending in zeros by multiplying non-zero parts and counting zeros.
Rudra gave 2 unaided correct responses out of 3 attempts on this method.
Practised using powers of 10 to judge product size and digit count; the response was unaided incorrect.
Rudra repeatedly overcounted zeros in examples such as 3,000 × 400; this was not corrected by the last seen attempt.
Used estimation for 48 × 1,020, giving approximately 50,000.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the method of multiplying the non-zero parts first and then counting the trailing zeros. Rudra correctly used this approach in some examples, including 500 × 80 and 2,500 × 40, but mixed up zeros when the non-zero product already contained zeros, such as 3,000 × 400; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, practise a few examples by writing the non-zero product separately and adding only the zeros from the original factors.
